discovery: The optical lattice clock: magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms enabling optical frequency standards at the 10^-18 level

nominees.name: Hidetoshi Katori
nominees.affiliation: University of Tokyo and RIKEN, Japan

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

subfield: Atomic physics / precision measurement and optical metrology
motivation: Katori conceived the optical lattice clock (2001-2005): trapping thousands of neutral atoms in an optical lattice at a 'magic' wavelength where the light shift of the clock transition cancels. This broke with the dogma that trapping fields must perturb the atomic reference, combining the Lamb-Dicke regime with a large atom number. Ye turned the concept into the world's most precise and accurate clocks, through ultrastable cavity-locked lasers, frequency-comb-based comparisons, control of atomic interactions and many-body effects, and systematic uncertainties now below 10^-18. Lattice clocks have measured the gravitational redshift over millimetre height differences, set new limits on variations of fundamental constants and on dark matter, enabled relativistic geodesy, and are driving the redefinition of the SI second. They are a culmination of the frequency-comb revolution recognized in 2005 and a new instrument for fundamental physics.
